newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 14.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick asks for "urgent explanations" over use of wiretappings from magistrates in La Spezia. Flick also opened an inquiry over comments made by some Milan magistrates, who accused politicans of inactivity in the face of corruption and cast doubts over the finance police (all).
* Parliamentary debate called over the electronic bugbing device found in the office of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi (all).
* Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti says he is ready to talk on constitutional reforms as long as it does not mean more powers to the president (Repubblica).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi is expected to present the 1997 budget to his European colleagues today in Luxembourg (La Stampa).

* Felice Vitali, former general director of financial holding group Gemina gave himself up to the police along with two other former managers. Magistrates ordered their arrest on charges of false accounting (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
